Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}{e}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the indeterminate form $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}{{e}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}} & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{{[\operatorname{sec}⁡x]}^{′}}{{[{e}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{{e}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x}}{{e}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{1}{{e}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
